 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.44/2022 of Cottonpet Police Station, now being investigated by CID, Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 336, 406, 420 and 120B of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Chandrashekar, pending on the file of learned 4th ACMM Court, Nrupatunga Road, Bengaluru.

2. Heard Sri. H.S.Chandramouli, learned Senior Counsel for Smt. Keerthana Nagaraj, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. H.S.Shankar, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1.
He is innocent and law-abiding citizen.
He has not committed any offence as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
There is reasonable apprehension of being arrested.
Hence, he is before this Court.
He is the Managing Director of the Private Company, who is the successful Bidder, undertook construction of 128 PC Quarters in the year 2016.
As per the agreement, the project was completed on 03.08.2018.
There was default liability to maintain the building for a period of one year, which was also ended on 30.08.2019.
In all six different agencies have involved in construction of the building.
However, later it is stated that some cracks have developed in the wall.
There is indemnity clause in the agreement entered into between the parties.
However, informant lodged the first information invoking penal provisions, which are not at all attracted to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
The petitioner is responsible person who had undertaken construction of the building and complied with the terms of the agreement.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not required for custodial interrogation.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause-title to the petition.
He is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition in the interest of justice.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
Specific allegations are made against the petitioner in respect of the construction of police quarters.
He has not appeared before the Investigating Officer even after filing of the first information.
He is absconding since from the date of registration of the case.
If he is granted anticipatory bail, he may never turn up before the Investigating Officer and he may abscond or may commit similar offences, threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.

Hence,
he prays for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text:
In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 6.
The Executive Engineer of the Karnataka State Police Housing and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited filed the first information against the petitioner making specific allegations.

entities.text: Karnataka State Police Housing and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is alleged that the petitioner being the successful bidder, entered into an agreement with KSPH and IDC Limited in the year 2016 for construction of 128 police quarters.
Due to negligent and poor-quality construction, the building had cracks.
Huge sum was misappropriated while construction.
Admittedly, there was an agreement between the parties.
It is not made clear whether the complainant had taken recourse to civil remedy or not.
However, it is not the contention of the prosecution that the petitioner is required for custodial interrogation.

Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the apprehensions expressed by the learned High Court Government Pleader that the petitioner may abscond or may tamper or threaten the prosecution witnesses.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.44/2022 of Cottonpet Police Station, Bengaluru.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the court as and when required; and d.
The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by him.
